question: Should OpenClaw adopt local, container, reverse-proxy, and node-mode as its initial opt-in, release-tested hosting-profile catalog, including the trusted-proxy and paired-control requirements?
rationale: This is a new product and configuration contract, not a repair to established behavior. Implementation evidence cannot determine which operator postures OpenClaw should permanently support or promise.

options.title: Accept the four-profile catalog
options.body: Adopt the opt-in catalog after the dependent readiness and profile implementations provide packaged conformance proof.

options.title: Narrow the initial catalog
options.body: Approve only the lower-policy profiles now and defer reverse-proxy or node-mode until their trust and control boundaries are separately sponsored.

options.title: Keep readiness unprofiled
options.body: Retain the readiness proposal without standard support-profile names until a future operator-support contract is approved.

recommendation.title: Accept the four-profile catalog
recommendation.body: Adopt the opt-in catalog after the dependent readiness and profile implementations provide packaged conformance proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the identified author of the RFC and linked implementation stack and can route the requested design decision to the relevant product owners.
